title: Rochdale veterans breakfast club receives £500 donation from housebuilders
excerpt: The donation from Barratt and David Wilson Homes will help cover the club's running costs ahead of Remembrance Day.
body:
The Rochdale Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club has received a £500 donation from Barratt and David Wilson Homes to support its running costs. The donation comes just ahead of Remembrance Day, highlighting the company's commitment to supporting the local veterans community.

The breakfast club meets every Thursday at the Rochdale Town Hall Bistro, providing a space for veterans and serving personnel to gather, share experiences, and foster camaraderie. This donation will assist with food expenses for members, ensuring that the club can continue to operate effectively.

Dave Williamson, a director at Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Clubs, expressed gratitude for the support, noting that such contributions are vital for maintaining the club's activities.

Mr Williamson, the director of the Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club CIC, made a donation of £500 to the Rochdale Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club in July.

Claire Jarvis, managing director at David Wilson Homes North West, stated that the donation is part of a broader community support initiative aimed at helping veterans across the region.

The Rochdale club is part of a worldwide network of breakfast clubs dedicated to veterans, offering essential support and friendship to those who have served in the military. The donation will help ensure that the club remains a welcoming space for all members.
